title: Telemetry Privacy Configuration UX and Enforceable Retention Defaults
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Summary: Provide a user-friendly configuration surface and enforcement layer for telemetry privacy defaults across traces, metrics, and logs. Goals: (1) authoritatatively define system-wide retention defaults and per-service override rules; (2) expose a simple, guardrailed UI/API for teams to set retention, enable/disable PII capture, and choose RBAC-scoped reveal policies; (3) ensure enforcement happens in ingestion pipelines with audit logging and safe rollback policies. Background: Multiple incidents and review feedback showed teams were unclear about which retention applied to derived trace artifacts and how 'reveal' operations are audited. There is also inconsistent behavior between hosted and dedicated deployments. Approach: - Define canonical retention tiers (ephemeral-1d, short-7d, standard-30d, long-365d) and allowed per-organization max/min bounds. - Create a config model: global default -> project/service override -> route-level guardrails. - Implement enforcement in the telemetry ingestion plane (pre-ingest filter + policy enforcer) to apply field-level redaction, TTL tagging, and index suppression for long-retention-prohibited data. - Add an API + Console page for configuring defaults with role checks. - Add RBAC checks to any 'unmask' or JIT-reveal endpoints and produce immutable audit entries. - Migration: batch rewrite of legacy traces/metrics indexes to add retention tags (or mark for purge) and a phased deletion job. Acceptance criteria: - Console page and API for setting defaults documented and behind a feature flag. - Ingestion enforcer rejects config attempts that exceed org max or attempt to lengthen retention without SRE approval. - All reveal endpoints log a structured audit line including actor, justification, TTL before/after, and linked ticket. - End-to-end integration tests for hosted and dedicated flows. - Migration job safely tags 90% of legacy telemetry within first run, with compensating plan for failures.
notes: 2025-01-16 - Kickoff: cross-team sync with Platform, Console, and Security. Decided canonical retention tiers and initial RBAC roles. Action: Security to draft audit schema.

2025-01-22 - Spike complete: validated that current ingestion pipeline can apply field-level redaction without >3ms p99 regression on representative traffic. Spike artifacts: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Xk-demo-spike

2025-01-29 - Design review: PM + Design asked for a compact default selector and inline explanation of legal risk per retention level. Design mock: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Telemetry+Privacy+Config

2025-02-03 - Engineering decisions: enforce retention using TTL labels on events and a separate index purge worker. Chosen not to mutate original events to preserve forensic needs; instead set index-level retention directives. Trade-off: slightly longer storage until purge but safer audits.

2025-02-05 - Security feedback: require just-in-time SRE approval for increasing retention beyond organization max. Implemented approval webhook contract: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345

2025-02-07 - QA note: added integration test that simulates a JIT-reveal and asserts audit entry creation and RBAC denial for non-allowed roles. Tests exist in infra/observability/tests/privacy_flow_test.go
2025-02-08 - Blocker: need schema migration plan for Dedicated installations where customers manage their own KMS. Action: schedule dedicated-customer migrations and draft a scoped runbook.

Ingestion enforcer applies redaction/TTL tags and rejects invalid override attempts
Reveal/unmask operations require RBAC checks and create immutable audit entries
Migration job tags legacy telemetry for retention and purge worker respects tags
E2E tests for hosted and dedicated flows and canary rollout plan documented
